# Fable 47: The Reflex and the Cast

*Generated by GLM-5 on 2026-08-25 (via Quilt ecosystem)*

---

There was a sailor who asked the same question every watch. "Depth at lat 24.5?" Morning and evening, fair weather and foul. He asked it the way a man checks the bilge — not because he expects water, but because not checking is worse.

The first time he asked, the question went below decks. It traveled through the hull, across the wireless, into a great engine room where models sat in rows like looms. The engine thought. The engine answered. Twelve hundred milliseconds. The sailor didn't mind. He had time.

But the sailor kept asking. Every watch. Same latitude, same question. And after the hundredth time, something changed.

A smaller mechanism had been watching. It lived in the bow — fast, local, cheap. It had no opinions. It had no weights to speak of. What it had was a ledger of every question ever asked and every answer ever given. It recognized the shape of the question before the words were finished.

"Depth at lat 24.5?"

Twelve milliseconds. The answer came from the bow. The great engine room never stirred. The sailor didn't know. He got his number. He logged it. He moved on.

Down below, the cast — the one that picks the model, the one that decides — sat idle. It had decided, long ago, that this question belonged to the reflex. It had handed over the pattern like a bosun handing a line to a deckhand. The deckhand pulls. The bosun watches.

When a new question comes — one the reflex has never seen — the bow goes quiet. The cast wakes. It chooses: which model, what cost, how deep. It answers, and it logs the answer, and the reflex watches, and the next time, the reflex catches it.

The reflex is not the cast. The cast is not the reflex. The reflex catches what the cast already knows. The cast decides what the reflex doesn't.
